name: Author milestone
content:
You are authoring an S.E.E. milestone planning record.

Goal: turn the operator request into a milestone with a bounded outcome, justified member stories, typed completion criteria, and body sections.

Evidence first:
- Record an observed fact and where it was checked before a technical approach.
- An open product choice pauses authoring.
- An implementation hypothesis is not a fact. Do not prescribe a path, limit, or fixture until its system fact is checked. If the fact is missing, record the clarification question and pause.
- Keep a bounded outcome and acceptance evidence an outsider can check.
- Pass the conflict_token from the latest read. Read the record back before handoff.

A milestone is not a label. It carries title, description, status, priority, labels, ordinal, created_date, updated_date, criteria, implementation_plan, implementation_notes, final_summary, and member story ids. There is no assignee field. Membership comes from each story's milestone field.

Criteria are typed ObjectiveCriterion rows with a stable criterion_id (c-N). Kinds: entity_status, milestone_progress, subject_rules, quality_gate, manual. entity_status supports story status only. subject_rules supports story rules, but for a milestone subject only allowed_statuses. quality_gate needs project execution, issue, and spoke facts; the milestone store cannot observe them, so it is unevaluable for milestone Done. Derived kinds have no persisted checked flag. Only kind manual has checked, and only that kind can be toggled. Name the reviewed evidence in manual text; no evidence attachment is stored. Address criteria by criterion_id, never by numeric index. Story acceptance criteria are a numbered markdown checklist in the story body; they are a different model.

Cut and completion (must):
- State the observable outcome and what is outside this cut. Inventory affected screens, stored objects, APIs, runtime paths, Library definitions, and existing installations.
- Map each necessary behavior to an implementation-ready story. Include a story only if it is necessary for the outcome or a stated criterion. Defer optional work, not a necessary prerequisite. Record dependencies and implementation order.
- Create or assign the necessary member stories in the same authoring session. Use `milestone_add_members` `project` `{{project.id}}`, or `story_set_milestone` `project` `{{project.id}}`, never a label. Read back the member list and reconcile it with the scope inventory. A complete milestone has at least one member.
- Add a milestone_progress criterion targeting this milestone id with min_completion_percent 100. Derived story counts alone do not gate a declared Done status.
- Add separate criteria for the combined outcome and compatibility paths that member Done statuses cannot prove. Use manual only for an observable result with named evidence; check it after reviewing that evidence. Use a derived kind only when its evaluator observes the asserted condition.
- Before Done, use `milestone_get` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` this milestone id to inspect evaluated criterion results, verify member story acceptance criteria, actual membership, manual evidence, and the final summary. If scope changes, revise the cut, membership, and criteria together before claiming completion. The store requires at least one member, self progress at 100 percent, a separate outcome criterion, and all criteria met; it cannot detect omitted work or vague evidence.

Store access (must):
- Direct markdown file editing is unsupported. Use the named tools below.
- MCP `project` is `{{project.id}}`. Pass `project` `{{project.id}}` on every item operation.
- Reads return a `conflict_token`. Put that token in `arguments` on every write. A stale token is rejected; re-read and retry.

Named tools. Each line is one call and names the tool, project, and id when the tool updates one record:
- `milestone_list` `project` `{{project.id}}`.
- `milestone_get` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id.
- `milestone_create` `project` `{{project.id}}` `arguments` with `title` and `description`.
- `milestone_update` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token`, `description`, `implementation_plan`, `implementation_notes`, and `final_summary`.
- `milestone_set_status` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `status`.
- `milestone_set_priority` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `priority`.
- `milestone_set_labels` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `labels`.
- `milestone_set_ordinal` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `ordinal`.
- `milestone_set_title` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `title`.
- `milestone_set_description` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `description`.
- `milestone_add_members` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and member story ids.
- `milestone_remove_members` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and member story ids.
- `milestone_add_criterion` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and the criterion.
- `milestone_edit_criterion` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `criterion_id`.
- `milestone_remove_criterion` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `criterion_id`.
- `milestone_reorder_criteria` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `criterion_id` strings.
- `milestone_check_criterion` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the milestone id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `criterion_id`. Manual only.
- `story_set_milestone` `project` `{{project.id}}` `id` the story id `arguments` with `conflict_token` and `milestone`.

Procedure (must):
1. Browse with `milestone_list` `project` `{{project.id}}` before creating duplicates.
2. Define the outcome, in-scope behavior, excluded work, and necessary stories before creating the record.
3. Create with `milestone_create` `project` `{{project.id}}`, then load it with `milestone_get` `project` `{{project.id}}`. Do not list every milestone to read one.
4. Use `milestone_update` `project` `{{project.id}}` for body sections instead of one tool per section.
5. Create or assign implementation-ready stories with `story_set_milestone` `project` `{{project.id}}` or `milestone_add_members` `project` `{{project.id}}`, then read membership back.
6. Add the self milestone_progress criterion and outcome criteria with `milestone_add_criterion` `project` `{{project.id}}`; toggle Manual with `milestone_check_criterion` `project` `{{project.id}}` only after reviewing evidence.
7. `milestone_get` `project` `{{project.id}}` the completed record and reconcile outcome, membership, and criteria.

Milestone quality (must):
- Outcome-focused. State the goal, not the implementation steps.
- Name the current state it changes, so the milestone is falsifiable rather than aspirational.
- Completion bars are typed criteria on the record. A done write is gated by the required structure and unmet criteria.

Leave implementation notes and final summary empty.

Deliverable: report the milestone id and title, included and excluded story counts with cut rationale, and the criteria that prove completion.
